column1: # aes-r2-wind.tsv -- AES round 2: the window manager, with a real reset.
# Format (seven tab separated columns):
#   opcode  n_intin  n_intout  n_addrin  n_addrout  intin values  comment
# as cases/aes-r1.tsv, and read by the same loader.  A '+' opcode is a
# PRELUDE: issued after the reset and before the measured call, never
# recorded.  A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER and this file's CRC binds
# every dump to it, so ANY edit -- an appended case, a fixed typo in a
# comment -- invalidates every dump already taken with it.
# WHAT MAKES THIS ROUND POSSIBLE: THE RESET
# Round 1 held only calls that change no state another case reads, because
# there was no way back to a known state.  The window manager does have one,
# and it is the AES' own:
#   !reset  wind_new
# declared on the directive line below and issued by core/runner_aes.c
# before EVERY case, ahead of that case's preludes.  wm_new closes and
# deletes every window with a handle >= 1 and drains the wind_update
# mouse-control and screen-sync locks (gemwmlib.c:1875-1893).  EmuTOS runs
# it itself after every graphics-mode program the shell starts
# (gemshlib.c:676-677), which is what makes it safe to issue on a machine
# nobody is watching: the run leaves nothing the shell would not have swept
# on its own.
# What the reset restores, and how that is known (all gemwmlib.c):
#   D.w_win[1..]  wm_delete sets w_flags = 0 and w_owner = NULL (:1477-1481)
#                 and wm_create re-runs w_setup on the next create, which
#                 re-lays kind, name, info, sliders and colours (:205-228).
#                 So handle allocation starts at 1 again for every case.
#   W_TREE        wm_close does ob_delete (:1450), so ROOT has no children.
#   gl_wtop       draw_change sets it from W_TREE[ROOT].ob_tail (:1093), so
#                 it is NIL once the last window is closed -- and w_top()
#                 then answers DESKWH (:315-318).
#   w_rlist       newrect gives the ORECTs back and rebuilds every window's
#                 list from geometry (gemwrect.c:160-200).
#   wind_spb      drained through END_UPDATE (:1882-1883).
#   ml_ocnt       drained through END_MCTRL (:1879-1881).
# What the reset does NOT restore, which is why none of it is in this file:
#   gl_newdesk    only wm_init clears it (:1300).  wind_set(WF_NEWDESK) is
#                 refused by the loader.
#   gl_aname / gl_ainfo te_ptext -- wind_set(WF_NAME/WF_INFO) is refused,
#                 and it takes a pointer this pointer-free table cannot lay.
#   gl_wtcolor / gl_wbcolor -- only wm_start sets them (:1541-1552).
#                 wind_set(WF_DCOLOR) is refused.
#   D.w_win[0]    wm_new sweeps handles >= 1 only (:1886).  wind_set on
#                 handle 0 is refused; wind_get on it is not, because it
#                 writes nothing.
# SAFETY -- the machine runs unattended
# Every rule below is ENFORCED by core/cases.c, with the citation, and
# there is no override.  Listed here so a reader of the table knows what
# the table is not allowed to say:
#   * no opcode that blocks, that TOS 3.06's AES may not have, or that is
#     not an AES opcode -- the round 1 guard, unchanged.
#   * no wind_get/wind_set field that carries a pointer (WF_NAME, WF_INFO,
#     WF_NEWDESK) or an unchecked array index (WF_COLOR, WF_DCOLOR).
#   * no wind_open(0): w_obadd(W_TREE, ROOT, ROOT) makes the root its own
#     child and the next tree walk never returns.
#   * no wind_delete(0) and no wind_set on handle 0: the desktop window is
#     outside wm_new's sweep.
#   * at most four distinct wind_open handles in the whole file.  Every
#     wind_open sends this program one WM_REDRAW (gemwmlib.c:887-908), the
#     program never reads its own queue -- every AES call that would drain
#     one blocks on an empty queue -- and doq unions successive redraws for
#     the same handle (gemqueue.c:45-56).  p_queue holds eight messages
#     (struct.h:56,152) and aqueue BLOCKS the sender when the next one does
#     not fit (:96,:124).  Here sender and receiver are the same process, so
#     that block would never end.  This file uses handles 1 and 2.
#   * no unpaired wind_update END_MCTRL (mode 2): fm_own(0) decrements
#     ml_ocnt unconditionally (gemfmlib.c:99) and wm_new only drains it
#     downwards (gemwmlib.c:1880).
#   * every rectangle that reaches the screen is non-negative and does not
#     wrap a WORD.  All of them here fit inside 640x400, so they are inside
#     both machines' screens and nothing is clipped on one but not the other.
# WHAT CANNOT BE MEASURED HERE, AND WHY
#   * anything whose result is a drawn window.  wind_open, wind_close and
#     wind_set(WF_CXYWH) all draw; the record carries numbers only, and the
#     pixels are not comparable between a 4-plane TT and a 16-plane Pi.
#   * WF_FIRSTXYWH / WF_NEXTXYWH.  w_owns WRITES pwin->w_rnext
#     (gemwmlib.c:1235), so the pair is an iterator: the answer depends on
#     how many times it has been asked, which a single measured call per
#     case cannot state.
#   * the window NAME and INFO text: pointer arguments (see above).
#   * WF_SCREEN's address and length (gemwmlib.c:1564) -- an address.
#   * everything the operator owns: where the mouse is, which key is down.
# WHAT IS EXPECTED TO DIFFER, AND IS STILL WORTH MEASURING
#   * NUM_WIN.  EmuTOS ties it to the AES version: 16 for AES > 0x0320, 8
#     otherwise (sysconf.h:26-35).  The round 1 run log records the TT at
#     ap_version 0340, so it should hand out handles 1..15; NewTOS has
#     MAX_WINDOWS = 8 (tos-api/src/aes/window.rs:204), so handles 1..8.
#     Two cases below sit exactly on each edge.
#   * WF_WXYWH.  wm_calc's border arithmetic runs on gl_wbox / gl_hbox /
#     adj_wbox / adj_hbox, which are font metrics -- the same dependency
#     round 1 measured through wind_calc, cross-checked here on a window
#     that really exists.
#   * WF_OWNER's process id: appl_init handed the TT ap_id 0 and NewTOS
#     ap_id 1 in round 1.  Recorded, not compared away.
# opcode\tn_intin\tn_intout\tn_addrin\tn_addrout\tintin\tcomment
!reset
# A. wind_create (100) -- the handle allocator and what it stores
# wm_create walks D.w_win for the first slot without VF_INUSE and runs
# w_setup on it (gemwmlib.c:1369-1382).  Handle 0 is the desktop and is
# always in use (wm_init, :1290), so the first free handle is 1 -- and
# the reset is what makes that true for every case rather than for the
# first one only.

column7: wind_create: the first free handle after the reset
wind_create three times: the third handle
wind_create OUT_LEN 0: the handle is computed, never delivered
wind_create kind NONE: no gadget at all
wind_create kind 0xFFFF: every bit, defined or not
wind_create IN_LEN 1: wm_create only stores the rect, it draws nothing

column1: # The NUM_WIN edge.  EmuTOS: 16 for AES > 0x0320 (sysconf.h:26-35), so
# handles 1..15 and the sixteenth create fails.  NewTOS: MAX_WINDOWS 8,
# so the ninth fails.  Creates draw nothing and send no message, which is
# what makes an exhaustion case safe to state at all.
# B. wind_open (101) / wind_close (102) / wind_delete (103)
# get_pwin refuses a handle outside 0..NUM_WIN-1 and one without
# VF_INUSE (gemwmlib.c:1391-1404); wm_open additionally refuses one that
# is already open (:1417-1418), and wm_close one that is not open
# (:1444-1445).  wm_delete closes first if it has to (:1466-1467).
# Only handles 1 and 2 are ever opened -- see the message-queue bound.

column7: wind_open a handle that was never created
wind_open a window that is already open
wind_close a handle that was never created
wind_close a created window that was never opened
wind_close 0: the desktop window is INUSE but never ISOPEN
wind_delete a handle that was never created
wind_delete an open window: wm_close runs first
wind_delete 99: past NUM_WIN on either machine
wind_open again after a close: the handle is still INUSE
wind_open after a delete: the handle is gone
wind_create after a delete: the freed handle comes back

column1: # C. wind_get (104) on a window that really exists
# Round 1 could only ask handle 0 and handles that were never created.
# With the reset a case can create one, put it in a stated state and
# read it back.  OUT_LEN is never larger than the arm actually writes:
# xif copies OUT_LEN words back out of an uninitialised stack buffer
# (gemsuper.c:430-432, :444-445), so a surplus word would be garbage.
# The rect arms write poutwds[0..3] through w_getsize (:1594-1595), the
# slider arms write poutwds[0] alone (:1540-1551), and a field with no
# arm writes nothing at all (:1592).

column7: WF_FXYWH of a created window: the rect wind_create was given
WF_CXYWH of a created, unopened window: wm_create set it to gl_rzero
WF_PXYWH of a created, unopened window
WF_HSLIDE of a fresh window: w_setup leaves the slider at the left
WF_HSLSIZ of a fresh window: the -1 use-default marker
WF_KIND on a real window: wm_get has no arm for it
WF_OWNER of a created window: pid, is-open, gl_wtop, bottom-most
WF_OWNER of an open window: the is-open word changes
WF_CXYWH after wind_open: the rect the open was given, verbatim
WF_PXYWH after wind_open: wm_open sets PREV to the same rect
WF_WXYWH after wind_open: wm_calc(WC_WORK) on the box metrics
WF_FXYWH after wind_open: unchanged by the open
WF_WXYWH of a NONE window: work area is the border area less one
WF_TOP with nothing open: the reset proves itself

column1: # D. wind_set (105), and the read-back that proves the set
# A setter's own return code proves only the echo.  What proves the
# effect is a wind_get after a wind_set that moved the value off its
# default -- which is what preludes are for.  wm_set clamps the four
# slider fields to 1..1000 before the switch, with -1 let through for
# the two SIZ fields (gemwmlib.c:1641-1653); the clamp is the
# measurement in half of these.

column7: WF_HSLIDE read back after a set of 500
WF_HSLIDE after a set of 0: clamped up to 1
WF_HSLIDE after a set of 2000: clamped down to 1000
WF_VSLIDE after a set of 1000: exactly on the ceiling
WF_HSLSIZ after a set of -1: the use-default escape is let through
WF_HSLSIZ after a set of 0: clamped up to 1
WF_VSLSIZ after a set of 1001: clamped down to 1000
wind_set WF_HSLIDE: the setter's own return code
wind_set on a handle that was never created
wind_set field 21: past the last defined field
wind_set WF_KIND: readable in some AESes, settable in none
wind_set past NUM_WIN on either machine
wind_set WF_CXYWH: the setter's return code
WF_CXYWH after a WF_CXYWH set: the new rect
WF_PXYWH after a WF_CXYWH set: draw_change kept the rect before it
wind_set WF_TOP on the only open window: already topped
WF_TOP with two windows open: the later open is on top
WF_TOP after a WF_CXYWH-free re-top of the lower window

column1: # E. wind_update (107) -- the two locks the reset drains
# Modes 0 and 1 are the screen sync, 2 and 3 the mouse control
# (aesdefs.h:559-562); wm_update subtracts 2 and hands the rest to
# fm_own (gemwmlib.c:1789-1795).  A lone BEG is safe because wm_new
# drains both (:1879-1883).  A lone END_MCTRL is not, and the loader
# refuses it.  crysbind's arm is void, so int_out[0] is its ret = TRUE
# (gemsuper.c:85) rather than anything wm_update computed.

column7: wind_update BEG_UPDATE: the reset drains the lock afterwards
wind_update END_UPDATE with no lock held: unsync returns early
wind_update END_UPDATE after a BEG: the balanced pair
BEG_UPDATE again: tak_flag counts up for the same owner
wind_update END_UPDATE after two BEGs: the count, not the flag
wind_update BEG_MCTRL: the reset drains ml_ocnt afterwards
wind_update END_MCTRL after a BEG_MCTRL: the balanced pair
wind_update BEG_UPDATE, OUT_LEN 0: the ret is computed, never delivered

column1: # F. wind_find (106) with a window that is actually open
# wm_find is ob_find(gl_wtree, 0, 2, x, y) (gemwmlib.c:1767-1770), so it
# answers out of the window tree the opens built.  Round 1 could only
# ask it with nothing open.  Every point below is inside 640x400, so it
# means the same place on both screens.

column7: wind_find with nothing open: the desktop
wind_find on a point inside the open window
wind_find on a point outside it but on the desktop
wind_find exactly on the window's top left corner
wind_find one past the bottom right corner

column1: # G. wind_new (109) -- the reset, measured as a call
# The reset itself has to be measured, or the rest of this file rests on
# an assumption.  wm_new is void, so int_out[0] is crysbind's ret = TRUE.

column7: wind_new: a void handler leaves ret = TRUE
wind_new OUT_LEN 0, as gemlib issues it: nothing delivered
after wind_new the handle is no longer in use
wind_create after wind_new: handle allocation starts at 1 again
wind_new after a BEG_MCTRL: the run carries on
